source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Durham campus publishes 40 MW of IT capacity, which is 80 percent of all data center power disclosed in North Carolina.

That concentration is a fact about disclosure as much as about hardware. Nineteen data centers are mapped in the state, and only five publish a power figure. Those five total 50 MW, so a single operator's two-building campus, DUR1 and DUR2, defines most of what is publicly known about data center load in North Carolina. The 420,000 square feet of technical space is the other concrete number attached to it.

For AI specifically, 40 MW is a real but bounded quantity. It is the kind of load a large campus draws, not the kind a frontier training cluster draws, and nothing in the published specifications says what share of it serves AI workloads rather than conventional colocation. The state's disclosed 50 MW is small against the grid build-out that would be required if AI demand keeps rising, but that comparison rests on a disclosed total that covers a minority of mapped sites.

What the data does not cover is substantial. There are no certifications listed, no street address, no coordinates, no announced expansion, and no tenant mix or utilization. The suitability score of 69 is computed only from published IT capacity and operator type, and it flags announced expansion as missing. Power supply agreements, interconnection status, and actual consumption are absent, so the campus can be sized but not assessed as an AI asset.
